\((\vec a+\vec b)\times(\vec a-\vec b)=\vec a\times\vec a-\vec a\times\vec b+\vec b\times\vec a-\vec b\times\vec b=-2(\vec a\times\vec b)\), since \(\vec a\times\vec a=\vec b\times\vec b=\vec 0\) and \(\vec b\times\vec a=-\vec a\times\vec b\).
Compute \(\vec a\times\vec b=\begin{vmatrix}\hat i&\hat j&\hat k\\2&3&-1\\1&-4&2\end{vmatrix}=\hat i(6-4)-\hat j(4+1)+\hat k(-8-3)=2\hat i-5\hat j-11\hat k\).
So \((\vec a+\vec b)\times(\vec a-\vec b)=-2(2\hat i-5\hat j-11\hat k)=\mathbf{-4\hat i+10\hat j+22\hat k}\).

Let \(\vec a=\hat j+2\hat k\) and \(\vec b=\hat i+\hat j\). A vector perpendicular to both is \(\vec a\times\vec b\).
\(\vec a\times\vec b=\begin{vmatrix}\hat i&\hat j&\hat k\\0&1&2\\1&1&0\end{vmatrix}=\hat i(0-2)-\hat j(0-2)+\hat k(0-1)=-2\hat i+2\hat j-\hat k\).
\(|\vec a\times\vec b|=\sqrt{4+4+1}=3\).
Required unit vectors \(=\pm\dfrac{1}{3}(-2\hat i+2\hat j-\hat k)\).

We know \(\vec a\cdot\vec b=|\vec a||\vec b|\cos\theta\) and \(|\vec a\times\vec b|=|\vec a||\vec b|\sin\theta\), so \(\tan\theta=\dfrac{|\vec a\times\vec b|}{\vec a\cdot\vec b}\).
\(|\vec a\times\vec b|=|2\hat i+\hat j+2\hat k|=\sqrt{4+1+4}=3\).
\(\tan\theta=\dfrac{3}{\sqrt3}=\sqrt3\Rightarrow\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{3}=60^\circ\).

A vector perpendicular to both \(\vec a\) and \(\vec b\) is along \(\vec a\times\vec b\).
\(\vec a\times\vec b=\begin{vmatrix}\hat i&\hat j&\hat k\\2&1&-3\\1&-2&1\end{vmatrix}=\hat i(1-6)-\hat j(2+3)+\hat k(-4-1)=-5\hat i-5\hat j-5\hat k=-5(\hat i+\hat j+\hat k)\).
\(|\vec a\times\vec b|=5\sqrt3\), so a unit vector along it is \(\pm\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}(\hat i+\hat j+\hat k)\).
Required vectors of magnitude 5 \(=\pm\dfrac{5}{\sqrt3}(\hat i+\hat j+\hat k)\).

\(|\vec u\times\vec v|=|\vec u||\vec v|\sin\theta\Rightarrow 8=2\cdot5\cdot\sin\theta\Rightarrow\sin\theta=\dfrac{4}{5}\), so \(\cos\theta=\pm\dfrac{3}{5}\).
\(\vec u\cdot\vec v=|\vec u||\vec v|\cos\theta=10\left(\pm\dfrac35\right)=\mathbf{\pm 6}\).

\(\vec u\cdot\vec v=|\vec u||\vec v|\cos\theta\Rightarrow 12=10\cdot2\cdot\cos\theta\Rightarrow\cos\theta=\dfrac{3}{5}\), so \(\sin\theta=\dfrac45\) (taking \(\theta\) acute since \(\cos\theta>0\)).
\(|\vec u\times\vec v|=|\vec u||\vec v|\sin\theta=20\left(\dfrac45\right)=\mathbf{16}\).

\(2(\vec a-\vec b)\times2(\vec a+\vec b)=4\big[(\vec a-\vec b)\times(\vec a+\vec b)\big]\)
\(=4\big[\vec a\times\vec a+\vec a\times\vec b-\vec b\times\vec a-\vec b\times\vec b\big]=4\big[\vec 0+\vec a\times\vec b+\vec a\times\vec b-\vec 0\big]\) (since \(\vec b\times\vec a=-\vec a\times\vec b\))
\(=4\cdot2(\vec a\times\vec b)=\mathbf{8(\vec a\times\vec b)}\). Hence proved.

\(\vec b+\vec c=5\hat i-4\hat j+3\hat k\).
\(\vec a\times(\vec b+\vec c)=\begin{vmatrix}\hat i&\hat j&\hat k\\1&-2&3\\5&-4&3\end{vmatrix}=\hat i(-6+12)-\hat j(3-15)+\hat k(-4+10)=6\hat i+12\hat j+6\hat k\).
\(\vec a\times\vec b=\begin{vmatrix}\hat i&\hat j&\hat k\\1&-2&3\\4&-3&1\end{vmatrix}=\hat i(-2+9)-\hat j(1-12)+\hat k(-3+8)=7\hat i+11\hat j+5\hat k\).
\(\vec a\times\vec c=\begin{vmatrix}\hat i&\hat j&\hat k\\1&-2&3\\1&-1&2\end{vmatrix}=\hat i(-4+3)-\hat j(2-3)+\hat k(-1+2)=-\hat i+\hat j+\hat k\).
\(\vec a\times\vec b+\vec a\times\vec c=(7-1)\hat i+(11+1)\hat j+(5+1)\hat k=6\hat i+12\hat j+6\hat k\).
Both sides equal \(6\hat i+12\hat j+6\hat k\), so \(\vec a\times(\vec b+\vec c)=\vec a\times\vec b+\vec a\times\vec c\) is verified.

\(\vec a\times\vec b=\begin{vmatrix}\hat i&\hat j&\hat k\\2&-2&1\\1&-3&-3\end{vmatrix}=\hat i(6+3)-\hat j(-6-1)+\hat k(-6+2)=9\hat i+7\hat j-4\hat k\).
Area \(=|\vec a\times\vec b|=\sqrt{81+49+16}=\mathbf{\sqrt{146}}\) sq. units.

Let \(\vec a,\vec b,\vec c,\vec d\) be the position vectors of A, B, C, D. Diagonal AC splits quadrilateral ABCD into \(\triangle ABC\) and \(\triangle ACD\).
Using the vector-area-of-a-triangle result, Area\((\triangle ABC)=\dfrac12(\vec a\times\vec b+\vec b\times\vec c+\vec c\times\vec a)\) and Area\((\triangle ACD)=\dfrac12(\vec a\times\vec c+\vec c\times\vec d+\vec d\times\vec a)\).
Adding, \(\vec c\times\vec a\) and \(\vec a\times\vec c\) cancel (they are negatives of each other), giving
Vector area of ABCD \(=\dfrac12(\vec a\times\vec b+\vec b\times\vec c+\vec c\times\vec d+\vec d\times\vec a)\).
Now \(\overline{AC}\times\overline{BD}=(\vec c-\vec a)\times(\vec d-\vec b)=\vec c\times\vec d-\vec c\times\vec b-\vec a\times\vec d+\vec a\times\vec b=\vec a\times\vec b+\vec b\times\vec c+\vec c\times\vec d+\vec d\times\vec a\) (using \(-\vec c\times\vec b=\vec b\times\vec c\), \(-\vec a\times\vec d=\vec d\times\vec a\)).
Hence vector area of ABCD \(=\dfrac12(\overline{AC}\times\overline{BD})\). Hence proved.

Let \(\vec a,\vec b,\vec c\) be the position vectors of A, B, C, so \(\overline{AB}=\vec b-\vec a\), \(\overline{AC}=\vec c-\vec a\).
\(\overline{AB}\times\overline{AC}=(\vec b-\vec a)\times(\vec c-\vec a)=\vec b\times\vec c-\vec b\times\vec a-\vec a\times\vec c+\vec a\times\vec a\).
Since \(\vec a\times\vec a=\vec 0\), \(-\vec b\times\vec a=\vec a\times\vec b\), and \(-\vec a\times\vec c=\vec c\times\vec a\):
\(\overline{AB}\times\overline{AC}=\vec a\times\vec b+\vec b\times\vec c+\vec c\times\vec a\).
Hence Area\((\triangle ABC)=\dfrac12|\overline{AB}\times\overline{AC}|=\mathbf{\dfrac12\big[\vec a\times\vec b+\vec b\times\vec c+\vec c\times\vec a\big]}\). Hence proved.

Let \(A(a,0,0)\), \(B(0,b,0)\), \(C(0,0,c)\).
\(\overline{AB}=-a\hat i+b\hat j\), \(\overline{AC}=-a\hat i+c\hat k\).
\(\overline{AB}\times\overline{AC}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat i&\hat j&\hat k\\-a&b&0\\-a&0&c\end{vmatrix}=\hat i(bc-0)-\hat j(-ac-0)+\hat k(0+ab)=bc\,\hat i+ac\,\hat j+ab\,\hat k\).
\(|\overline{AB}\times\overline{AC}|=\sqrt{b^2c^2+a^2c^2+a^2b^2}\).
Unit vector perpendicular to the plane \(=\mathbf{\dfrac{bc\,\hat i+ac\,\hat j+ab\,\hat k}{\sqrt{a^2b^2+b^2c^2+c^2a^2}}}\).
Area of triangle \(=\dfrac12|\overline{AB}\times\overline{AC}|=\mathbf{\dfrac12\sqrt{a^2b^2+b^2c^2+c^2a^2}}\).

Expand each term using the distributive law of the cross product:
\((\vec a+\vec b+\vec c)\times\vec c=\vec a\times\vec c+\vec b\times\vec c\) (since \(\vec c\times\vec c=\vec 0\)).
\((\vec a+\vec b+\vec c)\times\vec b=\vec a\times\vec b+\vec c\times\vec b=\vec a\times\vec b-\vec b\times\vec c\) (since \(\vec b\times\vec b=\vec 0\), \(\vec c\times\vec b=-\vec b\times\vec c\)).
\((\vec b+\vec c)\times\vec a=\vec b\times\vec a+\vec c\times\vec a=-\vec a\times\vec b-\vec a\times\vec c\).
Adding all three terms:
\((\vec a\times\vec c+\vec b\times\vec c)+(\vec a\times\vec b-\vec b\times\vec c)+(-\vec a\times\vec b-\vec a\times\vec c)=\vec 0\)
since \(\vec a\times\vec c\) cancels with \(-\vec a\times\vec c\), \(\vec b\times\vec c\) cancels with \(-\vec b\times\vec c\), and \(\vec a\times\vec b\) cancels with \(-\vec a\times\vec b\).
So the given left-hand side reduces identically to \(\vec 0\) for every choice of \(\vec a,\vec b,\vec c\). [Textbook misprint: the printed right-hand side \(2\vec a\times\vec c\) is incorrect — verified against the source page image, the transcription is faithful, but the claimed identity does not hold for any vectors (it always simplifies to \(\vec 0\)); the true identity is \((\vec a+\vec b+\vec c)\times\vec c+(\vec a+\vec b+\vec c)\times\vec b+(\vec b+\vec c)\times\vec a=\vec 0\).]

No, not necessarily. \(\vec a\times\vec b=\vec a\times\vec c\Rightarrow\vec a\times(\vec b-\vec c)=\vec 0\). Since \(\vec a\ne\vec 0\), this only forces \(\vec b-\vec c\) to be parallel to \(\vec a\) (i.e. \(\vec b-\vec c=\lambda\vec a\) for some scalar \(\lambda\)); it does not force \(\vec b-\vec c=\vec 0\).
Counter-example: let \(\vec a=\hat i\), \(\vec b=\hat j\), \(\vec c=\hat i+\hat j\). Then \(\vec a\times\vec b=\hat i\times\hat j=\hat k\) and \(\vec a\times\vec c=\hat i\times(\hat i+\hat j)=\hat i\times\hat i+\hat i\times\hat j=\hat k\). So \(\vec a\times\vec b=\vec a\times\vec c\) although \(\vec b\ne\vec c\). \(\mathbf{Answer: No}\).

From \(\vec a\times\vec b=\vec a\times\vec c\): \(\vec a\times(\vec b-\vec c)=\vec 0\Rightarrow\vec b-\vec c=\lambda\vec a\) for some scalar \(\lambda\) (as in part (b), since \(\vec a\ne\vec 0\)).
From \(\vec a\cdot\vec b=\vec a\cdot\vec c\): \(\vec a\cdot(\vec b-\vec c)=0\). Substituting \(\vec b-\vec c=\lambda\vec a\):
\(\vec a\cdot(\lambda\vec a)=\lambda|\vec a|^2=0\).
Since \(\vec a\ne\vec 0\), \(|\vec a|^2\ne0\), so \(\lambda=0\), giving \(\vec b-\vec c=\vec 0\), i.e. \(\mathbf{\vec b=\vec c}\). \(\mathbf{Answer: Yes}\).

Let \(\vec a=3\hat i+2\hat j-\hat k\), \(\vec b=-2\hat i+2\hat j-3\hat k\), \(\vec c=3\hat i+5\hat j-2\hat k\), \(\vec d=-2\hat i+5\hat j-4\hat k\) be the position vectors of A, B, C, D.
(i) \(\overline{AB}=\vec b-\vec a=-5\hat i-2\hat k\) and \(\overline{CD}=\vec d-\vec c=-5\hat i-2\hat k\), so \(\overline{AB}=\overline{CD}\) — AB is parallel and equal in length to CD.
Also \(\overline{AC}=\vec c-\vec a=3\hat j-\hat k\) and \(\overline{BD}=\vec d-\vec b=3\hat j-\hat k\), so \(\overline{AC}=\overline{BD}\) as well.
Both pairs of opposite sides being equal and parallel confirms that A, B, D, C (taken in this cyclic order) form a parallelogram; equivalently, its diagonals AD and BC bisect each other at \(\left(\dfrac12,\dfrac72,-\dfrac52\right)\), the common midpoint of AD and BC. Hence verified.
(ii) Area \(=|\overline{AB}\times\overline{AC}|\) (using the two sides meeting at A):
\(\overline{AB}\times\overline{AC}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat i&\hat j&\hat k\\-5&0&-2\\0&3&-1\end{vmatrix}=\hat i(0+6)-\hat j(5-0)+\hat k(-15-0)=6\hat i-5\hat j-15\hat k\).
Area \(=\sqrt{36+25+225}=\mathbf{\sqrt{286}}\) sq. units.

Let \(\vec a,\vec b,\vec c,\vec d\) be position vectors of A, B, C, D.
\(\overline{AB}\times\overline{CD}=(\vec b-\vec a)\times(\vec d-\vec c)=\vec b\times\vec d-\vec b\times\vec c-\vec a\times\vec d+\vec a\times\vec c\)
\(\overline{BC}\times\overline{AD}=(\vec c-\vec b)\times(\vec d-\vec a)=\vec c\times\vec d-\vec c\times\vec a-\vec b\times\vec d+\vec b\times\vec a\)
\(\overline{CA}\times\overline{BD}=(\vec a-\vec c)\times(\vec d-\vec b)=\vec a\times\vec d-\vec a\times\vec b-\vec c\times\vec d+\vec c\times\vec b\)
Adding all three, the \(\vec b\times\vec d\), \(\vec c\times\vec d\), and \(\vec a\times\vec d\) terms cancel in pairs, leaving
Sum \(=-2(\vec b\times\vec c)+2(\vec a\times\vec c)-2(\vec a\times\vec b)=-2(\vec a\times\vec b+\vec b\times\vec c+\vec c\times\vec a)\).
By Q.32, Area\((\triangle ABC)=\dfrac12|\vec a\times\vec b+\vec b\times\vec c+\vec c\times\vec a|\), i.e. \(|\vec a\times\vec b+\vec b\times\vec c+\vec c\times\vec a|=2\,\text{area}(\triangle ABC)\).
Hence \(|\overline{AB}\times\overline{CD}+\overline{BC}\times\overline{AD}+\overline{CA}\times\overline{BD}|=2\times2\,\text{area}(\triangle ABC)=\mathbf{4\,\text{area}(\triangle ABC)}\). Hence proved.

Since \(\hat a\cdot\hat b=0\) and \(\hat a\cdot\hat c=0\), \(\hat a\) is perpendicular to both \(\hat b\) and \(\hat c\); hence \(\hat a\) is parallel to \(\hat b\times\hat c\) (as \(\hat b\) and \(\hat c\) are non-parallel, their angle being \(\pi/6\)). So \(\hat a=\lambda(\hat b\times\hat c)\) for some scalar \(\lambda\).
\(|\hat b\times\hat c|=|\hat b||\hat c|\sin\dfrac{\pi}{6}=1\cdot1\cdot\dfrac12=\dfrac12\).
Since \(\hat a\) is a unit vector, \(|\hat a|=|\lambda|\cdot|\hat b\times\hat c|=|\lambda|\cdot\dfrac12=1\Rightarrow|\lambda|=2\Rightarrow\lambda=\pm2\).
Hence \(\mathbf{\hat a=\pm2(\hat b\times\hat c)}\). Hence proved.
